quiz.0.question: When designing a wine list with real depth for Italian wines, beyond the 'three pillars (Piemonte, Tuscany, Veneto)', what elements do sommeliers typically add to demonstrate expertise?
quiz.0.options.1: Hidden gem regions (Campania, Friuli, Alto Piemonte), older vintages and unusual indigenous varieties
quiz.0.explanation: A sophisticated Italian wine list goes beyond the classics to include: southern Italian gems (Taurasi, Greco di Tufo), Friuli whites, Alto Piemonte Nebbiolo, interesting indigenous varieties and older vintages — signalling genuine depth of knowledge.
quiz.1.question: What pricing strategy do modern restaurants most commonly use to encourage customers to trade up to premium wines while maintaining entry-level margins?
quiz.1.options.1: Regressive scaling — high markup percentage on entry-level, lower percentage (but higher absolute margin) on premium wines
quiz.1.options.2: Fixed percentage markup for all wines
quiz.1.explanation: Regressive scaling: entry-level wines carry a higher percentage markup (e.g., ×4–5 wholesale cost); premium wines carry a lower percentage (e.g., ×2–3) — making expensive bottles more attractive while ensuring the restaurant profits adequately at every level.
quiz.2.question: What is the industry's most common 'golden rule' for BTG pricing?
quiz.2.options.0: Price at the same level as bottled wine
quiz.2.options.1: One glass (usually 150ml) = the wholesale bottle cost — meaning the whole bottle's revenue covers the bottle cost on the first glass
quiz.2.options.2: Price at double the bottled wine per-glass equivalent
quiz.2.options.3: Price based solely on what the market will bear
quiz.2.explanation: The BTG golden rule: price one glass at approximately the wine's wholesale cost — so the first pour covers your cost, and remaining glasses are profit. A standard 750ml bottle yields approximately 5 glasses.
quiz.3.question: If a restaurant wants to offer very expensive wines by the glass (e.g., a $50 glass of aged Barolo) without worrying about unsold glasses oxidising, what is the most effective solution?
quiz.3.options.1: Use a Coravin wine preservation system — extract wine without removing the cork
quiz.3.options.2: Re-cork the bottle and refrigerate immediately
quiz.3.options.3: Only pour the wine for parties of 4 or more
quiz.3.explanation: Coravin uses a thin needle to extract wine through the cork, replacing it with argon gas — the cork reseals naturally. This allows restaurants to offer premium aged wines by the glass without committing to opening the full bottle.
